back: A word that describes a noun or pronoun, giving more information about it.
notes: a **tall** tree; the road is **dusty**; she seems **happy**.

back: One syllable: add -er/-est (tall, taller, tallest). Two syllables ending in -y: -ier/-iest (busy, busier, busiest). Longer adjectives: more/most (more careful, most careful).
notes: Never combine them: not 'more taller' or 'most hottest'.

back: good, better, best; bad, worse, worst; little, less, least; much/many, more, most; far, farther/further, farthest/furthest.
-ing describes the thing that causes a feeling (a boring lesson); -ed describes how a person feels (bored pupils).
Opinion – size – age – shape – colour – origin – material – purpose – noun.
notes: a lovely small old round red Zimbabwean clay cooking pot (normally use no more than three).

back: An adjective that describes an all-or-nothing state, so it cannot be made stronger or weaker with very or more.
notes: dead, unique, impossible, perfect, empty: use completely or absolutely, not very.

back: Use as + adjective + as for equality: Tendai is as tall as his father. The negative is not as/so ... as.
notes: This exercise is not as difficult as the last one.

front: Comparing one with the rest of its group
back: Say taller than any other girl in the team, not taller than any girl in the team, when the person is part of that group.
